head: e5117658841ca30d4b888f311754c8818f06dbf3
maintainer_decision: Decide the expected commit/DBQ semantics after an incomplete flush, and whether a stalled client should freeze RF accounting for later successful responses. The real callback was released after stall processing; the exact snapshot/clear race and cluster recovery remain unproven.
prior_r10_assessment: r10's focused suite passed 10/10 at seeds 5330 and 5330C0DE and its five fail-before mutations behaved as expected. Its real 200/503 callback test ran blockUntilFinished after callbacks, and the synthetic error-drain interleaving did not prove a real concurrent callback race. Its root forbiddenApisTest failed on three Executors.* test calls, an independent CI cleanup item.
recommendation: Keep the minimal error-collection fix, but define and test the ordered-flush behavior when a stream stalls. Preserve a guard that prevents later ordered operations crossing an incomplete flush while still retaining errors; drain-and-rethrow is one observed policy, not the only possible safe design. Review the fork callback fence separately because it suppresses later successful callbacks and changes the shared test RF tracker.
summary: The original lost-other-replica-error premise reproduces on pinned base 0ea013e and passes on contributor head eedcb534. The contributor DBQ probe then submitted a DBQ between two queued older updates. The optional fork comparison retained errors and rethrew before commit/DBQ submission, preserving order in the fixture.
title: PR 5330 premise audit: error recovery and ordered updates
